subject: Sovereign storage & TTL options — roadmap request
messages:
From: Miguel Sánchez <miguel.sanchez@finsight.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finsight.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sovereign storage & TTL questions + ask for roadmap

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. We loved the throughput numbers, but before procurement can move forward we need clear answers on a couple of items around data residency and deletion:

- Can Redwood support per-tenant regional residency (store customer data exclusively in a US sovereign bucket)?
- Is configurable retention possible at the project/tenant level (we need 7 years for some datasets; 30 days for others)?
- What deletion guarantees exist (hard delete vs soft delete, audit trail, deletion webhooks)?
- Can we get a timeline for where this sits on your roadmap and a rough delivery ETA?

I've attached a spreadsheet with our retention matrix and compliance notes. Procurement would like a short mutual action plan (MAP) that maps your deliverables and target dates so they can align legal and SOC2 evidence collection.

Can you loop in product & eng? Happy to do a quick call next week.

Best,
Miguel
Miguel Sánchez
Head of IT Risk, Finsight Capital

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Sovereign storage & TTL questions + ask for roadmap

Hi Miguel — thanks for the clear matrix, that helps a lot. Looping in Jasmine (product) and Karthik (engineering) to scope and propose a MAP.

Quick answers upfront while we scope:
- We already support region-aware routing for inference, but durable object storage residency per-tenant is not fully GA.
- We do have deletion APIs and soft-delete flows today, but they are global and not per-region/tenant.
- Audit logs exist for admin actions but we need to confirm exportable proof of deletion for compliance use-cases.

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal scoping call (30m) with product + eng + your security team — propose Tue 6/1 or Wed 6/2.
2) We’ll produce a MAP linking your spreadsheet rows to implementation options and an estimated timeline.
3) Delivery tiers: quick win (tenant-level residency + default TTL override), targeted (per-dataset TTL + deletion provenance), advanced (per-region immutable retention + certified evidence).

I've attached a short design note and asked Karthik to sketch effort estimates. Do these tiers align with Finsight's needs?

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart

Subject: Re: Sovereign storage & TTL questions + ask for roadmap

Thanks — adding engineering constraints and a proposed timeline. High level:

- Current state: inference routing can pin requests to regions; model KV/cache is ephemeral and fine. Persistent customer artifacts (index/embeddings, long-term logs, backups) are stored in a global S3-backed tier.

- Effort to support per-tenant sovereign storage: approx 6–8 weeks engineering (design + infra + migrations) to enable a per-tenant storage namespace and region pinning for durable artifacts. This includes:
  * metadata isolation (tenant->storage mapping)
  * provisioning per-region buckets with encryption keys (KMS integration)
  * backup/restore and retention enforcement layer

- Effort to support configurable TTLs per-dataset: another 3–4 weeks after the storage work to add TTL metadata, scheduled expirer service, and audit logs for deletions.

- Challenges: snapshots/backups across regions and third-party archival (cold storage) will need policy work; this can add time depending on compliance requirements.

Proposed phased delivery:
Phase 0 (2 weeks): finalize data model and compliance acceptance criteria; produce MAP
Phase 1 (6–8 weeks): tenant-level sovereign storage + defaults for TTL
Phase 2 (3–4 weeks): per-dataset TTL + deletion provenance + webhooks
Phase 3 (4+ weeks): advanced immutable retention policies and SOC2 evidence pack automation

I’ll put a short RFC on the docs folder after the scoping call.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Platform

Miguel — thanks for the matrix and context. A few product notes to add:

- API: we can expose retention_days and residency_region as part of the CreateProject / UpdateProject endpoints. Backward-compatible default will be no change.
- Console: add route (Project Settings > Data Residency) with dropdown for region selection and simple TTL presets (30d, 90d, 1y, 7y) + custom.
- Deletion guarantees: we will provide a deletion-provenance record (timestamp, actor, request-id) and a deletion webhook so you can reconcile programmatically.
- Notifications: include an expiry notification option at 30/10/1 days before retention lapse.

Risks/notes: encrypted backups and cold archives may be retained by our backup provider for a short reconciliation window; we need to confirm retention windows with infra. That will be part of the compliance acceptance criteria.

Action items for our side:
- Karthik to produce phase estimates (done above) and RFC.
- I will draft the MAP and an initial timeline after the scoping call and share a Drive doc.

Proposed scoping call: Tue 6/1 10:00 AM PT. Miguel, does that work for you?

—Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Product Manager — Data Platform, Redwood Inference
